exercises.title: An adjacency list
exercises.task: Read Graph: a map from each node to the list of nodes it points to. Run builds a small food web (fox -> rabbit means the fox eats the rabbit), prints what each species eats, then the reverse graph: who eats it.

exercises.title: Build the graph
exercises.task: Fill Build: read lines A -> B and add the edge. Every node that appears, even only on the right, must be a key of the graph, with an empty list if it points nowhere.
hints: Make sure B exists as a key too: if _, ok := g[b]; !ok { g[b] = nil }.
Then g[a] = append(g[a], b): appending to a missing key works, it starts from nil.

exercises.title: Producers and apex predators
exercises.task: In a food web, list the producers (species that eat nothing: plants, algae) and the apex predators (species that nothing eats). Both lists sorted.
hints: Producer: the node's own list is empty.
Apex predator: it never appears in anyone's list. Count the incoming edges (the in-degree) in a map.
sort.Strings before returning: map iteration order is random.
